title: PyTorch: tensors, autograd, modules and the training loop

videos.script: For eight lessons, every backward pass in this course was written by hand. {{numpy}} This lesson hands that work to PyTorch, and checks that it did it right. {{tensor}} A tensor is a NumPy array that knows where it lives. It can also record the arithmetic done to it. {{record}} Give it lesson 3's tiny network, call backward once, and the same gradients come back. {{same}} A module holds its own weights. A network of two layers here has 2,410 of them. {{count}} Then the training loop, in five lines: forward, loss, zero the gradients, backward, step. {{five}} Thirty epochs on the digits reach 0.950 on the validation set. {{run}} Most mistakes in such a loop do not crash. They print numbers that look almost reasonable. {{bugs}} Leave out one line, and the loss climbs instead of falling. {{climb}} Add one softmax too many, and the network stops learning at about one in five. {{softmax}} Each of five classic bugs is run here, so you know its symptom when you meet it. {{symptom}} Last, the weights go into a file and come back out, with the same score. {{end}}
